amendments.because: Listing every test in the new fix's Done-when duplicates next's lines and grows without limit; the fix names the failed run instead
amendments.done_when: When the latest nightly full run failed, forge next names the platforms and failing tests and gives the forge fix start command for them

done_when: When the latest scheduled run of a workflow failed, forge next names its failed jobs and every failing test, and gives one forge fix start command for that failed run (or the started fix's next step)

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 3, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. `gh workflow list` defaults to 50 results, so a failed scheduled workflow outside that first page is never checked or shown. Also, `src/forge/nextstep.py:282` keys alerts by a cleaned workflow name: two workflows with the same display name, or names that clean to the same text, collapse into one alert and one fix command. The named proof has only two differently named workflows. [GitHub CLI documents the 50-workflow default](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_workflow_list).

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 3, Harm 2
The parser at this line recognizes only pytest-style `FAILED` or `ERROR` lines containing `::`. Scheduled Jest, Vitest and Go test jobs can fail with named tests in their logs but no matching line, so `forge next` shows the job without those tests. The shipped guidance supports these runners in `src/forge/templates/skill.md:730` and `:1153`. This is an additional language case.
findings.title: Follow-up: name JavaScript and Go test failures in scheduled runs

stop.reason: Coordinator (Harm 2, reversible): the generated fix names the failed jobs and the run, not every test (forge next's lines already name every test); a fix started on another machine gets the plain line that it runs on that machine, like other remote items.

why: A failing nightly full run on macOS or Windows is easy to miss, and Windows stayed red for days unseen
